# Resource: stripe_terminal_reader

A Stripe Terminal card reader registered at a location. `terraform destroy` deletes the reader. Only `label` and `metadata` change in place: changing the `location` or the `registration_code` creates a new reader. In test mode the registration code `simulated-wpe` registers a simulated reader. The reader's `action` reports the most recent action it performed; the resource does not start actions, and the nested objects of an action's API error are not available.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_terminal_location" "store" {
  display_name = "Main Street store"

  address = {
    line1       = "354 Oyster Point Blvd"
    city        = "South San Francisco"
    state       = "CA"
    postal_code = "94080"
    country     = "US"
  }
}

# Enter the code the reader shows when you register it. In test mode, `simulated-wpe`
# registers a simulated reader.
resource "stripe_terminal_reader" "counter" {
  registration_code = "simulated-wpe"
  location          = stripe_terminal_location.store.id
  label             = "Front counter"

  metadata = {
    lane = "1"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `registration_code` - (Required) A code generated by the reader used for registering to an account. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `label` - (Optional) Custom label given to the reader for easier identification. If no label is specified, the registration code will be used. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `location` - (Optional) The location to assign the reader to. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `action` - The most recent action performed by the reader. See [`action`](#action) below.
* `device_sw_version` - The current software version of the reader.
* `device_type` - Device type of the reader. Possible values: `bbpos_chipper2x`, `bbpos_wisepad3`, `bbpos_wisepos_e`, `mobile_phone_reader`, `simulated_stripe_s700`, `simulated_stripe_s710`, `simulated_verifone_m425`, `simulated_verifone_p630`, `simulated_verifone_ux700`, `simulated_verifone_v660p`, `simulated_wisepos_e`, `stripe_m2`, `stripe_s700`, `stripe_s710`, `verifone_P400`, `verifone_m425`, `verifone_p630`, `verifone_ux700`, `verifone_v660p`.
* `ip_address` - The local IP address of the reader.
* `last_seen_at` - The last time this reader reported to Stripe backend. Timestamp is measured in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Unlike most other Stripe timestamp fields which use seconds, this field uses milliseconds.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `serial_number` - Serial number of the reader.
* `status` - The networking status of the reader. This value is `null` for mobile readers. We do not recommend using this field in flows that may block taking payments. Possible values: `offline`, `online`.

<a id="action"></a>
### `action`

The `action` attribute supports:

* `api_error` - The reader action failed due to an [API error](https://docs.stripe.com/api/errors). Only present when `status` is `failed` and the underlying failure was an API error. Avoid parsing the `message` field for programmatic logic; use `type` or `code` instead. The `message` field is for display to humans only and may be updated at anytime. Requires [reader version](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-reader-s700-s710#reader-software-version) 2.42 or later. Readers on older versions always return null. See [`action.api_error`](#action.api_error) below.
* `collect_inputs` - Represents a reader action to collect customer inputs See [`action.collect_inputs`](#action.collect_inputs) below.
* `collect_payment_method` - Represents a reader action to collect a payment method See [`action.collect_payment_method`](#action.collect_payment_method) below.
* `confirm_payment_intent` - Represents a reader action to confirm a payment See [`action.confirm_payment_intent`](#action.confirm_payment_intent) below.
* `failure_code` - Failure code, only set if status is `failed`.
* `failure_message` - Detailed failure message, only set if status is `failed`.
* `print_content` - Represents a reader action to print content See [`action.print_content`](#action.print_content) below.
* `process_payment_intent` - Represents a reader action to process a payment intent See [`action.process_payment_intent`](#action.process_payment_intent) below.
* `process_setup_intent` - Represents a reader action to process a setup intent See [`action.process_setup_intent`](#action.process_setup_intent) below.
* `refund_payment` - Represents a reader action to refund a payment See [`action.refund_payment`](#action.refund_payment) below.
* `set_reader_display` - Represents a reader action to set the reader display See [`action.set_reader_display`](#action.set_reader_display) below.
* `status` - Status of the action performed by the reader. Possible values: `failed`, `in_progress`, `succeeded`.
* `type` - Type of action performed by the reader. Possible values: `collect_inputs`, `collect_payment_method`, `confirm_payment_intent`, `print_content`, `process_payment_intent`, `process_setup_intent`, `refund_payment`, `set_reader_display`.

<a id="action.api_error"></a>
### `action.api_error`

The `action.api_error` attribute supports:

* `advice_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating [how to proceed with an error](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/card#retrying-issuer-declines) if they provide one.
* `charge` - For card errors, the ID of the failed charge.
* `code` - For some errors that could be handled programmatically, a short string indicating the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.
* `decline_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating the [card issuer's reason for the decline](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#issuer-declines) if they provide one.
* `doc_url` - A URL to more information about the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.
* `message` - A human-readable message providing more details about the error. For card errors, these messages can be shown to your users.
* `network_advice_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice given to merchant by the card network on how to proceed with an error.
* `network_decline_code` - For payments declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the payment failed.
* `param` - If the error is parameter-specific, the parameter related to the error. For example, you can use this to display a message near the correct form field.
* `payment_method` - PaymentMethod objects represent your customer's payment instruments. You can use them with [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents) to collect payments or save them to Customer objects to store instrument details for future payments. Related guides: [Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods) and [More Payment Scenarios](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/more-payment-scenarios). See [`action.api_error.payment_method`](#action.api_error.payment_method) below.
* `payment_method_type` - If the error is specific to the type of payment method, the payment method type that had a problem. This field is only populated for invoice-related errors.
* `request_log_url` - A URL to the request log entry in your dashboard.
* `type` - The type of error returned. One of `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, or `invalid_request_error` Possible values: `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, `invalid_request_error`.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.acss_debit"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.acss_debit`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `institution_number` - Institution number of the bank account.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `transit_number` - Transit number of the bank account.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.au_becs_debit"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.au_becs_debit`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.au_becs_debit` attribute supports:

* `bsb_number` - Six-digit number identifying bank and branch associated with this bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.bacs_debit"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.bacs_debit`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.bacs_debit` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `sort_code` - Sort code of the bank account. (e.g., `10-20-30`)

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - Billing address. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details.address`](#action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.
* `phone` - Billing phone number (including extension).
* `tax_id` - Taxpayer identification number. Used only for transactions between LATAM buyers and non-LATAM sellers.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details.address"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details.address`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

### `action.api_error.payment_method.bizum`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.bizum` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique identifier for the buyer as determined by the local payment processor.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.blik"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.blik`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.blik` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique and immutable identifier assigned by BLIK to every buyer.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.card"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.card`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `checks` - Checks on Card address and CVC if provided. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.checks`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.checks) below.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `display_brand` - The brand to use when displaying the card, this accounts for customer's brand choice on dual-branded cards. Can be `american_express`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners_club`, `discover`, `eftpos_australia`, `interac`, `jcb`, `mastercard`, `union_pay`, `visa`, or `other` and may contain more values in the future.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `generated_from` - Details of the original PaymentMethod that created this object. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from) below.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `networks` - Contains information about card networks that can be used to process the payment. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.networks`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.networks) below.
* `regulated_status` - Status of a card based on the card issuer. Possible values: `regulated`, `unregulated`.
* `three_d_secure_usage` - Contains details on how this Card may be used for 3D Secure authentication. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.three_d_secure_usage`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.three_d_secure_usage) below.
* `wallet` - If this Card is part of a card wallet, this contains the details of the card wallet. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.wallet`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.wallet) below.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.card.checks"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.checks`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.checks` attribute supports:

* `address_line1_check` - If a address line1 was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.
* `address_postal_code_check` - If a address postal code was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.
* `cvc_check` - If a CVC was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from` attribute supports:

* `charge` - The charge that created this object.
* `payment_method_details` - Transaction-specific details of the payment method used in the payment. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details) below.
* `setup_attempt` - The ID of the SetupAttempt that generated this PaymentMethod, if any.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `card_present` - See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present) below.
* `type` - The type of payment method transaction-specific details from the transaction that generated this `card` payment method. Always `card_present`.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present` attribute supports:

* `amount_authorized` - The authorized amount
* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `brand_product` - The [product code](https://stripe.com/docs/card-product-codes) that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.
* `capture_before` - When using manual capture, a future timestamp after which the charge will be automatically refunded if uncaptured.
* `cardholder_name` - The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `description` - A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.
* `emv_auth_data` - Authorization response cryptogram.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `generated_card` - ID of a card PaymentMethod generated from the card_present PaymentMethod that may be attached to a Customer for future transactions. Only present if it was possible to generate a card PaymentMethod.
* `incremental_authorization_supported` - Whether this [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents) is eligible for incremental authorizations. Request support using [request_incremental_authorization_support](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create#create_payment_intent-payment_method_options-card_present-request_incremental_authorization_support).
* `issuer` - The name of the card's issuing bank.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `network` - Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.
* `network_transaction_id` - This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `offline` - Details about payments collected offline. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline) below.
* `overcapture_supported` - Defines whether the authorized amount can be over-captured or not
* `preferred_locales` - The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `read_method` - How card details were read in this transaction. Possible values: `contact_emv`, `contactless_emv`, `contactless_magstripe_mode`, `magnetic_stripe_fallback`, `magnetic_stripe_track2`.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `receipt` - A collection of fields required to be displayed on receipts. Only required for EMV transactions. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt) below.
* `wallet` - See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet) below.

### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline` attribute supports:

* `stored_at` - Time at which the payment was collected while offline
* `type` - The method used to process this payment method offline. Only deferred is allowed. Possible values: `deferred`.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt` attribute supports:

* `account_type` - The type of account being debited or credited Possible values: `checking`, `credit`, `prepaid`, `unknown`.
* `application_cryptogram` - The Application Cryptogram, a unique value generated by the card to authenticate the transaction with issuers.
* `application_preferred_name` - The Application Identifier (AID) on the card used to determine which networks are eligible to process the transaction. Referenced from EMV tag 9F12, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `authorization_code` - Identifier for this transaction.
* `authorization_response_code` - EMV tag 8A. A code returned by the card issuer.
* `cardholder_verification_method` - Describes the method used by the cardholder to verify ownership of the card. One of the following: `approval`, `failure`, `none`, `offline_pin`, `offline_pin_and_signature`, `online_pin`, or `signature`.
* `dedicated_file_name` - Similar to the application_preferred_name, identifying the applications (AIDs) available on the card. Referenced from EMV tag 84.
* `terminal_verification_results` - A 5-byte string that records the checks and validations that occur between the card and the terminal. These checks determine how the terminal processes the transaction and what risk tolerance is acceptable. Referenced from EMV Tag 95.
* `transaction_status_information` - An indication of which steps were completed during the card read process. Referenced from EMV Tag 9B.

### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet` attribute supports:

* `type` - The type of mobile wallet, one of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, or `unknown`. Possible values: `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, `unknown`.

* `preferred` - The preferred network for co-branded cards. Can be `cartes_bancaires`, `mastercard`, `visa` or `invalid_preference` if requested network is not valid for the card.

### `action.api_error.payment_method.card.wallet`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card.wallet` attribute supports:

An additional hash is included on the Wallet subhash with a name matching this value. It contains additional information specific to the card wallet type. Possible values: `amex_express_checkout`, `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `link`, `masterpass`, `samsung_pay`, `visa_checkout`.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.card_present"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.card_present`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.card_present` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `brand_product` - The [product code](https://stripe.com/docs/card-product-codes) that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.
* `cardholder_name` - The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `description` - A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `issuer` - The name of the card's issuing bank.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `networks` - Contains information about card networks that can be used to process the payment. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card_present.networks`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card_present.networks) below.
* `offline` - Details about payment methods collected offline. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card_present.offline`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card_present.offline) below.
* `preferred_locales` - The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `read_method` - How card details were read in this transaction. Possible values: `contact_emv`, `contactless_emv`, `contactless_magstripe_mode`, `magnetic_stripe_fallback`, `magnetic_stripe_track2`.
* `wallet` - See [`action.api_error.payment_method.card_present.wallet`](#action.api_error.payment_method.card_present.wallet) below.

* `preferred` - The preferred network for the card.

Possible values: `alior_bank`, `bank_millennium`, `bank_nowy_bfg_sa`, `bank_pekao_sa`, `banki_spbdzielcze`, `blik`, `bnp_paribas`, `boz`, `citi_handlowy`, `credit_agricole`, `envelobank`, `etransfer_pocztowy24`, `getin_bank`, `ideabank`, `ing`, `inteligo`, `mbank_mtransfer`, `nest_przelew`, `noble_pay`, `pbac_z_ipko`, `plus_bank`, `santander_przelew24`, `tmobile_usbugi_bankowe`, `toyota_bank`, `velobank`, `volkswagen_bank`.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.paypal"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.paypal`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.paypal` attribute supports:

* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the buyer's country. Values are provided by PayPal directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.
* `payer_email` - Owner's email. Values are provided by PayPal directly (if supported) at the time of authorization or settlement. They cannot be set or mutated.
* `payer_id` - PayPal account PayerID. This identifier uniquely identifies the PayPal customer.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.payto"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.payto`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.payto` attribute supports:

* `bsb_number` - Bank-State-Branch number of the bank account.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `pay_id` - The PayID alias for the bank account.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.pix"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.pix`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.pix` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular Pix account. You can use this attribute to check whether two Pix accounts are the same.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.radar_options"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.radar_options`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.radar_options` attribute supports:

* `session` - A [Radar Session](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/radar-session) is a snapshot of the browser metadata and device details that help Radar make more accurate predictions on your payments.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit` attribute supports:

* `bank_code` - Bank code of bank associated with the bank account.
* `branch_code` - Branch code of bank associated with the bank account.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `generated_from` - Information about the object that generated this PaymentMethod. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit.generated_from`](#action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit.generated_from) below.
* `last4` - Last four characters of the IBAN.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit.generated_from"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit.generated_from`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.sepa_debit.generated_from` attribute supports:

* `charge` - The ID of the Charge that generated this PaymentMethod, if any.
* `setup_attempt` - The ID of the SetupAttempt that generated this PaymentMethod, if any.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.sofort"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.sofort`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.sofort` attribute supports:

* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.upi"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.upi`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.upi` attribute supports:

* `vpa` - Customer's unique Virtual Payment Address

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - The name of the bank.
* `financial_connections_account` - The ID of the Financial Connections Account used to create the payment method.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `networks` - Contains information about US bank account networks that can be used. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.networks`](#action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.networks) below.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.
* `status_details` - Contains information about the future reusability of this PaymentMethod. See [`action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details`](#action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details) below.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.networks"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.networks`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.networks` attribute supports:

* `preferred` - The preferred network.
* `supported` - All supported networks.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details` attribute supports:

* `blocked` - See [`action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details.blocked`](#action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details.blocked) below.

<a id="action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details.blocked"></a>
### `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details.blocked`

The `action.api_error.payment_method.us_bank_account.status_details.blocked` attribute supports:

* `network_code` - The ACH network code that resulted in this block. Possible values: `R02`, `R03`, `R04`, `R05`, `R07`, `R08`, `R10`, `R11`, `R16`, `R20`, `R29`, `R31`.
* `reason` - The reason why this PaymentMethod's fingerprint has been blocked Possible values: `bank_account_closed`, `bank_account_frozen`, `bank_account_invalid_details`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_account_unusable`, `debit_not_authorized`, `tokenized_account_number_deactivated`.

<a id="action.collect_inputs"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs`

The `action.collect_inputs` attribute supports:

* `inputs` - List of inputs to be collected. See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs) below.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `custom_text` - Default text of input being collected. See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.custom_text`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.custom_text) below.
* `email` - Information about a email being collected using a reader See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.email`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.email) below.
* `numeric` - Information about a number being collected using a reader See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.numeric`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.numeric) below.
* `phone` - Information about a phone number being collected using a reader See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.phone`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.phone) below.
* `required` - Indicate that this input is required, disabling the skip button.
* `selection` - Information about a selection being collected using a reader See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection) below.
* `signature` - Information about a signature being collected using a reader See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.signature`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.signature) below.
* `skipped` - Indicate that this input was skipped by the user.
* `text` - Information about text being collected using a reader See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.text`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.text) below.
* `toggles` - List of toggles being collected. Values are present if collection is complete. See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.toggles`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.toggles) below.
* `type` - Type of input being collected. Possible values: `email`, `numeric`, `phone`, `selection`, `signature`, `text`.

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.custom_text"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.custom_text`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.custom_text` attribute supports:

* `description` - Customize the default description for this input
* `skip_button` - Customize the default label for this input's skip button
* `submit_button` - Customize the default label for this input's submit button
* `title` - Customize the default title for this input

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.email"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.email`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.email` attribute supports:

* `value` - The collected email address

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.numeric"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.numeric`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.numeric` attribute supports:

* `value` - The collected number

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.phone"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.phone`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.phone` attribute supports:

* `value` - The collected phone number

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection` attribute supports:

* `choices` - List of possible choices to be selected See [`action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection.choices`](#action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection.choices) below.
* `id` - The id of the selected choice
* `text` - The text of the selected choice

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection.choices"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection.choices`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.selection.choices` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `id` - The identifier for the selected choice. Maximum 50 characters.
* `style` - The button style for the choice. Can be `primary` or `secondary`. Possible values: `primary`, `secondary`.
* `text` - The text to be selected. Maximum 30 characters.

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.signature"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.signature`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.signature` attribute supports:

* `value` - The File ID of a collected signature image

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.text"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.text`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.text` attribute supports:

* `value` - The collected text value

<a id="action.collect_inputs.inputs.toggles"></a>
### `action.collect_inputs.inputs.toggles`

The `action.collect_inputs.inputs.toggles` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `default_value` - The toggle's default value. Can be `enabled` or `disabled`. Possible values: `disabled`, `enabled`.
* `description` - The toggle's description text. Maximum 50 characters.
* `title` - The toggle's title text. Maximum 50 characters.
* `value` - The toggle's collected value. Can be `enabled` or `disabled`. Possible values: `disabled`, `enabled`.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method`

The `action.collect_payment_method` attribute supports:

* `collect_config` - Represents a per-transaction override of a reader configuration See [`action.collect_payment_method.collect_config`](#action.collect_payment_method.collect_config) below.
* `payment_intent` - Most recent PaymentIntent processed by the reader.
* `payment_method` - PaymentMethod objects represent your customer's payment instruments. You can use them with [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents) to collect payments or save them to Customer objects to store instrument details for future payments. Related guides: [Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods) and [More Payment Scenarios](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/more-payment-scenarios). See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method) below.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.collect_config"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.collect_config`

The `action.collect_payment_method.collect_config` attribute supports:

* `enable_customer_cancellation` - Enable customer-initiated cancellation when processing this payment.
* `skip_tipping` - Override showing a tipping selection screen on this transaction.
* `tipping` - Represents a per-transaction tipping configuration See [`action.collect_payment_method.collect_config.tipping`](#action.collect_payment_method.collect_config.tipping) below.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.collect_config.tipping"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.collect_config.tipping`

The `action.collect_payment_method.collect_config.tipping` attribute supports:

* `amount_eligible` - Amount used to calculate tip suggestions on tipping selection screen for this transaction. Must be a positive integer in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to represent $1.00 or 100 to represent ¥100, a zero-decimal currency).

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method` attribute supports:

* `acss_debit` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.acss_debit`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.acss_debit) below.
* `allow_redisplay` - This field indicates whether this payment method can be shown again to its customer in a checkout flow. Stripe products such as Checkout and Elements use this field to determine whether a payment method can be shown as a saved payment method in a checkout flow. The field defaults to “unspecified”. Possible values: `always`, `limited`, `unspecified`.
* `au_becs_debit` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.au_becs_debit`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.au_becs_debit) below.
* `bacs_debit` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bacs_debit`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bacs_debit) below.
* `billing_details` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details) below.
* `bizum` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bizum`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bizum) below.
* `blik` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.blik`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.blik) below.
* `boleto` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.boleto`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.boleto) below.
* `card` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card) below.
* `card_present` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present) below.
* `cashapp` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.cashapp`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.cashapp) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `custom` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.custom`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.custom) below.
* `customer` - The ID of the Customer to which this PaymentMethod is saved. This will not be set when the PaymentMethod has not been saved to a Customer.
* `customer_account` -
* `eps` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.eps`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.eps) below.
* `fpx` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.fpx`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.fpx) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `ideal` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.ideal`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.ideal) below.
* `interac_present` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.interac_present`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.interac_present) below.
* `klarna` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.klarna`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.klarna) below.
* `kr_card` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.kr_card`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.kr_card) below.
* `link` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.link`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.link) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `naver_pay` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.naver_pay`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.naver_pay) below.
* `nz_bank_account` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.nz_bank_account`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.nz_bank_account) below.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `payment_method`.
* `p24` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.p24`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.p24) below.
* `paypal` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.paypal`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.paypal) below.
* `payto` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.payto`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.payto) below.
* `pix` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.pix`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.pix) below.
* `radar_options` - Options to configure Radar. See [Radar Session](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/radar-session) for more information. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.radar_options`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.radar_options) below.
* `sepa_debit` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.sepa_debit`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.sepa_debit) below.
* `sofort` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.sofort`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.sofort) below.
* `type` - The type of the PaymentMethod. An additional hash is included on the PaymentMethod with a name matching this value. It contains additional information specific to the PaymentMethod type. Possible values: `acss_debit`, `affirm`, `afterpay_clearpay`, `alipay`, `alma`, `amazon_pay`, `au_becs_debit`, `bacs_debit`, `bancontact`, `billie`, `bizum`, `blik`, `boleto`, `card`, `card_present`, `cashapp`, `crypto`, `custom`, `customer_balance`, `eps`, `fpx`, `giropay`, `grabpay`, `ideal`, `interac_present`, `kakao_pay`, `klarna`, `konbini`, `kr_card`, `link`, `mb_way`, `mobilepay`, `multibanco`, `naver_pay`, `nz_bank_account`, `oxxo`, `p24`, `pay_by_bank`, `payco`, `paynow`, `paypal`, `paypay`, `payto`, `pix`, `promptpay`, `revolut_pay`, `samsung_pay`, `satispay`, `scalapay`, `sepa_debit`, `sequra`, `sofort`, `sunbit`, `swish`, `twint`, `upi`, `us_bank_account`, `wechat_pay`, `zip`.
* `upi` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.upi`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.upi) below.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.us_bank_account`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.acss_debit"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.acss_debit`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `institution_number` - Institution number of the bank account.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `transit_number` - Transit number of the bank account.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.au_becs_debit"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.au_becs_debit`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.au_becs_debit` attribute supports:

* `bsb_number` - Six-digit number identifying bank and branch associated with this bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bacs_debit"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bacs_debit`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bacs_debit` attribute supports:

* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `sort_code` - Sort code of the bank account. (e.g., `10-20-30`)

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - Billing address. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details.address`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.
* `phone` - Billing phone number (including extension).
* `tax_id` - Taxpayer identification number. Used only for transactions between LATAM buyers and non-LATAM sellers.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details.address"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details.address`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bizum"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bizum`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.bizum` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique identifier for the buyer as determined by the local payment processor.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.blik"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.blik`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.blik` attribute supports:

* `buyer_id` - A unique and immutable identifier assigned by BLIK to every buyer.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.boleto"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.boleto`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.boleto` attribute supports:

* `tax_id` - Uniquely identifies the customer tax id (CNPJ or CPF)

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `checks` - Checks on Card address and CVC if provided. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.checks`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.checks) below.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `display_brand` - The brand to use when displaying the card, this accounts for customer's brand choice on dual-branded cards. Can be `american_express`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners_club`, `discover`, `eftpos_australia`, `interac`, `jcb`, `mastercard`, `union_pay`, `visa`, or `other` and may contain more values in the future.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `generated_from` - Details of the original PaymentMethod that created this object. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from) below.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `networks` - Contains information about card networks that can be used to process the payment. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.networks`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.networks) below.
* `regulated_status` - Status of a card based on the card issuer. Possible values: `regulated`, `unregulated`.
* `three_d_secure_usage` - Contains details on how this Card may be used for 3D Secure authentication. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.three_d_secure_usage`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.three_d_secure_usage) below.
* `wallet` - If this Card is part of a card wallet, this contains the details of the card wallet. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet) below.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.checks"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.checks`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.checks` attribute supports:

* `address_line1_check` - If a address line1 was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.
* `address_postal_code_check` - If a address postal code was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.
* `cvc_check` - If a CVC was provided, results of the check, one of `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, or `unchecked`.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from` attribute supports:

* `charge` - The charge that created this object.
* `payment_method_details` - Transaction-specific details of the payment method used in the payment. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details) below.
* `setup_attempt` - The ID of the SetupAttempt that generated this PaymentMethod, if any.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `card_present` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present) below.
* `type` - The type of payment method transaction-specific details from the transaction that generated this `card` payment method. Always `card_present`.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present` attribute supports:

* `amount_authorized` - The authorized amount
* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `brand_product` - The [product code](https://stripe.com/docs/card-product-codes) that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.
* `capture_before` - When using manual capture, a future timestamp after which the charge will be automatically refunded if uncaptured.
* `cardholder_name` - The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `description` - A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.
* `emv_auth_data` - Authorization response cryptogram.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `generated_card` - ID of a card PaymentMethod generated from the card_present PaymentMethod that may be attached to a Customer for future transactions. Only present if it was possible to generate a card PaymentMethod.
* `incremental_authorization_supported` - Whether this [PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents) is eligible for incremental authorizations. Request support using [request_incremental_authorization_support](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create#create_payment_intent-payment_method_options-card_present-request_incremental_authorization_support).
* `issuer` - The name of the card's issuing bank.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the card.
* `location` - ID of the [location](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/locations) that this transaction's reader is assigned to.
* `network` - Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa`, or `unknown`.
* `network_transaction_id` - This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.
* `offline` - Details about payments collected offline. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline) below.
* `overcapture_supported` - Defines whether the authorized amount can be over-captured or not
* `preferred_locales` - The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `read_method` - How card details were read in this transaction. Possible values: `contact_emv`, `contactless_emv`, `contactless_magstripe_mode`, `magnetic_stripe_fallback`, `magnetic_stripe_track2`.
* `reader` - ID of the [reader](https://docs.stripe.com/api/terminal/readers) this transaction was made on.
* `receipt` - A collection of fields required to be displayed on receipts. Only required for EMV transactions. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt) below.
* `wallet` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet) below.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.offline` attribute supports:

* `stored_at` - Time at which the payment was collected while offline
* `type` - The method used to process this payment method offline. Only deferred is allowed. Possible values: `deferred`.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.receipt` attribute supports:

* `account_type` - The type of account being debited or credited Possible values: `checking`, `credit`, `prepaid`, `unknown`.
* `application_cryptogram` - The Application Cryptogram, a unique value generated by the card to authenticate the transaction with issuers.
* `application_preferred_name` - The Application Identifier (AID) on the card used to determine which networks are eligible to process the transaction. Referenced from EMV tag 9F12, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `authorization_code` - Identifier for this transaction.
* `authorization_response_code` - EMV tag 8A. A code returned by the card issuer.
* `cardholder_verification_method` - Describes the method used by the cardholder to verify ownership of the card. One of the following: `approval`, `failure`, `none`, `offline_pin`, `offline_pin_and_signature`, `online_pin`, or `signature`.
* `dedicated_file_name` - Similar to the application_preferred_name, identifying the applications (AIDs) available on the card. Referenced from EMV tag 84.
* `terminal_verification_results` - A 5-byte string that records the checks and validations that occur between the card and the terminal. These checks determine how the terminal processes the transaction and what risk tolerance is acceptable. Referenced from EMV Tag 95.
* `transaction_status_information` - An indication of which steps were completed during the card read process. Referenced from EMV Tag 9B.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.generated_from.payment_method_details.card_present.wallet` attribute supports:

* `type` - The type of mobile wallet, one of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, or `unknown`. Possible values: `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`, `unknown`.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.networks"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.networks`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.networks` attribute supports:

* `available` - All networks available for selection via [payment_method_options.card.network](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/confirm#confirm_payment_intent-payment_method_options-card-network).
* `preferred` - The preferred network for co-branded cards. Can be `cartes_bancaires`, `mastercard`, `visa` or `invalid_preference` if requested network is not valid for the card.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.three_d_secure_usage"></a>

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet` attribute supports:

* `dynamic_last4` - (For tokenized numbers only.) The last four digits of the device account number.
* `masterpass` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet.masterpass`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet.masterpass) below.
* `type` - The type of the card wallet, one of `amex_express_checkout`, `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `masterpass`, `samsung_pay`, `visa_checkout`, or `link`. An additional hash is included on the Wallet subhash with a name matching this value. It contains additional information specific to the card wallet type. Possible values: `amex_express_checkout`, `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `link`, `masterpass`, `samsung_pay`, `visa_checkout`.
* `visa_checkout` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet.visa_checkout`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet.visa_checkout) below.

They cannot be set or mutated. They cannot be set or mutated. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet.masterpass.shipping_address`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card.wallet.masterpass.shipping_address) below.

<a id="action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present"></a>
### `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present`

The `action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present` attribute supports:

* `brand` - Card brand. Can be `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `visa` or `unknown`.
* `brand_product` - The [product code](https://stripe.com/docs/card-product-codes) that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.
* `cardholder_name` - The cardholder name as read from the card, in [ISO 7813](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_7813) format. May include alphanumeric characters, special characters and first/last name separator (`/`). In some cases, the cardholder name may not be available depending on how the issuer has configured the card. Cardholder name is typically not available on swipe or contactless payments, such as those made with Apple Pay and Google Pay.
* `country` - Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.
* `description` - A high-level description of the type of cards issued in this range.
* `exp_month` - Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.
* `exp_year` - Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number. *As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.*
* `funding` - Card funding type. Can be `credit`, `debit`, `prepaid`, or `unknown`.
* `issuer` - The name of the card's issuing bank.

* `networks` - Contains information about card networks that can be used to process the payment. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present.networks`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present.networks) below.
* `offline` - Details about payment methods collected offline. See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present.offline`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present.offline) below.
* `preferred_locales` - The languages that the issuing bank recommends using for localizing any customer-facing text, as read from the card. Referenced from EMV tag 5F2D, data encoded on the card's chip.
* `read_method` - How card details were read in this transaction. Possible values: `contact_emv`, `contactless_emv`, `contactless_magstripe_mode`, `magnetic_stripe_fallback`, `magnetic_stripe_track2`.
* `wallet` - See [`action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present.wallet`](#action.collect_payment_method.payment_method.card_present.wallet) below.
